Day 1
From Hotel: 3 min · 2 min → Roman Theatre
1. Roman Theatre
A 1st-century BC theatre built under Augustus, buried for centuries and rediscovered during mid-20th-century roadworks. The cavea, orchestra pit, and stage backdrop survive in remarkable condition at the foot of the Alcazaba.
Read more

2. Alcazaba
An 11th-century Moorish fortress-palace with layered defensive walls, horseshoe arches, tranquil courtyards with flowing water, and sweeping views over the port and city from its ramparts.

27 min · 9 min → Castillo de Gibralfaro
3. Castillo de Gibralfaro
A 14th-century hilltop castle built by the Nasrid dynasty to protect the Alcazaba below. The walkable ramparts offer the best panoramic views in Málaga — the port, the bullring, the cathedral, and the coastline stretching toward Africa.
Read more

25 min · 15 min → Centre Pompidou Málaga
4. Centre Pompidou Málaga
The only Centre Pompidou outside France, housed beneath a striking multicolored glass cube on the port. The rotating collection draws from over 100 works by Picasso, Frida Kahlo, Francis Bacon, and Magritte.

Day 2
From Hotel: 8 min · 6 min → Málaga Cathedral
1. Málaga Cathedral
Known as La Manquita — the one-armed lady — for its unfinished south tower. This Renaissance cathedral took over 200 years to build and blends Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque styles under soaring 40-meter vaults.
Read more

7 min · 5 min → Picasso Museum
2. Picasso Museum
Housed in the 16th-century Palacio de Buenavista, this museum holds over 200 works spanning Picasso's career — from early academic sketches to late Cubist ceramics — in the city where he was born.

Day 3
From Hotel: 22 min → La Concepción Botanical Garden
1. La Concepción Botanical Garden
A 19th-century subtropical paradise in the hills north of the city, with over 2,000 plant species including towering palms, centuries-old wisteria, bamboo groves, and a romantic English-landscape design created by a marquis and his wife.
Read more
Tuesday - Sunday 9:30am - 8:30pm
Closed Monday
~1 hr 30 min
Camino del Jardín Botánico 3 · La Concepción
20 min → Basílica de Santa María de la Victoria
2. Basílica de Santa María de la Victoria
Málaga's patron saint basilica, built on the site where the Catholic Monarchs camped during the siege. The interior houses a lavishly decorated Camarín and a crypt with painted ceiling depicting death and the afterlife.
Tuesday - Friday 10:00am - 12:30pm · Tuesday - Friday 5:00pm - 7:30pm · Saturday 10:00am - 12:30pm

Plaza del Santuario · s/n · Victoria
11 min · 8 min → Iglesia de Santiago
3. Iglesia de Santiago
The oldest church in Málaga, built in the years immediately after the Christian reconquest. Its Mudéjar bell tower is one of three surviving in the city, and the baptismal font inside is where Pablo Picasso was christened.
Read more

4. Automobile and Fashion Museum
Almost 100 classic cars — Rolls-Royce, Bugatti, Ferrari, Hispano-Suiza — displayed alongside 200 haute couture pieces in 13 themed rooms inside the former Royal Tobacco Factory, a striking 1920s industrial building.

Local Tastes
Espetos
Sardines skewered on bamboo canes and grilled over open driftwood fires on the beach — Málaga's defining street food since the 19th century.
El Tintero · El Caleño
Ajoblanco
A cold soup made from raw almonds · garlic · bread · olive oil · and vinegar — a Moorish-era recipe predating gazpacho. Served with grapes or melon in summer.
El Pimpi · Cortijo de Pepe
Porra Antequerana
A thick cold tomato soup from nearby Antequera · denser than salmorejo · served with chopped egg and jamón. A summer staple in traditional bars.
Casa Lola · El Tapeo de Cervantes
Berenjenas con Miel
Thin-sliced aubergine · battered and fried crisp · then drizzled with sugarcane honey — a contrast of textures unique to Málaga province.
El Pimpi · Cortijo de Pepe
Málaga Dulce · Sweet Wine
A fortified muscatel wine with DO designation · aged in solera casks since the 18th century. Dark amber · raisin-rich · and intensely sweet.
Antigua Casa de Guardia
Food Delivery
Glovo
Foreign number: accepted — enter it with the country code and keep roaming on for the SMS code.
The dominant delivery platform in Málaga, covering restaurants, supermarkets and pharmacies across the centre; reliable choice for anything from tapas to groceries.
glovoapp.com
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted — it uses the same Uber account and number as the ride app.
Good selection of restaurants in the historic centre and La Malagueta; delivery windows in the city centre typically run 25–40 min and the app is straightforward for a first-time user.
ubereats.com
Just Eat
Foreign number: accepted.
Spain's longest-established delivery platform with a strong roster of independent local restaurants; useful for neighbourhood spots that are not on Glovo or Uber Eats.
just-eat.es
Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted.
The easiest option in Málaga for visitors; good coverage across the centre and the beach district, with consistent wait times and in-app payment that needs no cash or local card.
uber.com
Cabify
Foreign number: not accepted — requires a Spanish or European number to register.
Premium alternative to Uber with newer vehicles and professional drivers; registration requires a Spanish or European number, so it is not available to visitors without a local SIM.
cabify.com

Day Trips by Train
Antequera · 20 min
UNESCO-listed dolmens among Europe's oldest monumental structures. The town offers a Renaissance old town · the Alcazaba fortress · El Torcal's surreal limestone karst formations.
book at: Renfe · Omio
Fuengirola · 35 min
A relaxed Costa del Sol beach town by Cercanías rail — the Sohail Castle · the long promenade · the old fishermen's quarter for a slower-paced half-day alternative.
book at: Renfe · Omio
Córdoba · 1 hr
The Mezquita-Catedral — 856 double-arched columns in an endless forest of red-and-white striped stone. The Jewish Quarter and Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos are within distance.
book at: Renfe · Omio
Granada · 1 hr 30 min
The Alhambra palace complex — Nasrid Palaces · Generalife gardens · the Alcazaba fortress — set against the Sierra Nevada. The Albaicín quarter offers whitewashed streets and Mirador de San Nicolás views.
book at: Renfe · Omio
Seville · 2 hr
Spain's largest cathedral · the Real Alcázar palace complex · the sweeping Plaza de España — Seville's monumental center and vibrant Triana quarter across the river.
book at: Renfe · Omio
Ronda · 2 hr via Antequera
A dramatic clifftop town split by the El Tajo gorge · spanned by the Puente Nuevo. One of Spain's most scenic rail approaches through the Serranía de Ronda mountains.
book at: Renfe · Omio

Worth Knowing

The Picasso Thread

There's a quiet thread that runs through this trip. On Day 2 you'll stand in the Palacio de Buenavista looking at Picasso's earliest works — sketches he made as a child in this city. On Day 3 you'll walk into Iglesia de Santiago and find the exact baptismal font where he was christened Pablo Diego José Francisco de Paula Juan Nepomuceno María de los Remedios Cipriano de la Santísima Trinidad Ruiz y Picasso, shortly after his birth. The museum and the church are five minutes apart. One holds the art; the other holds the beginning.

The Alcazaba's double-walled design — where you walk between two parallel fortified walls before ever reaching the interior — was a defensive innovation that the Moors brought from Damascus. When Ferdinand and Isabella finally took Málaga after one of the longest sieges of the Reconquista, it wasn't the walls they broke through. They starved the city for three months. The Basílica de la Victoria on Day 3 was built on the exact camp where Ferdinand pitched his tent during that siege — the same spot where he made a vow to the Virgin if the city fell.
